results.title: Topology in Biological Piezoelectric Materials - CityU Scholars
results.content: Discovery of the piezoelectric eﬀect and the identiﬁcation of piezoelectric-ity in biological tissues highlight the gradual expansion of the ﬁeld.[1–4] The integration of topology has oﬀered new theoretical insights, enabling precise analysis of electric domain structures and inspiring innovative material designs with multifunctional capabilities.[16–23] Topology has become crucial for optimizing piezoelectric properties and advancing cross-domain applications.[24–28] Adapted with permission.[16,24] Copyright 1950, American Physics Society. Machine learning (ML), as a powerful data-driven method, has shown great potential in materials design and optimization in recent years, driving the shift of materials science from the tra-ditional experiment-driven paradigm to an intelligent and data-intensive paradigm.[151] With theoretical computational methods (e.g., high-throughput computing and density functional theory), ML algorithms can eﬃciently mine potential laws in complex data, rapidly predict structure-property relationships of materi-als, and reduce experimental and computational costs.[152] Es-pecially in the ﬁeld of piezoelectric materials, machine learning provides interpretable means to improve the piezoelectric coef-ﬁcient of materials.[153] For high-performance piezoelectric ma-terials based on aluminum nitrides, ML enabled high-precision prediction of AlN-based piezoelectric materials by learning the performance data of the materials at diﬀerent concentrations and compositions (Figure 13B).[154] Such research accelerates the dis-covery of high-performance materials.
